reference: Documented descriptor API contracts and Linux epoll readiness semantics for private pipes/FIFOs. There is no matching GNU persistent-descriptor CLI; network and signal behavior require separate reviewed mocks.
coverage: Bash reports bashpoll as an available builtin.
help bashpoll exposes the documented subcommand synopsis and descriptor/event contract.
wait returns successfully with empty output on a zero-timeout pipe with no read event, and reports writable for explicit write interests.
wait reports read readiness and hangup after a private pipe writer reaches EOF.
Unknown subcommands and invalid wait options use the documented usage status and produce diagnostics.
TCP, UNIX socket, UDP, signalfd, and injected descriptor lifecycle behavior is recorded as deferred pending isolated fixtures.
Private FIFO descriptor flag-setter/close and simultaneous two-descriptor readiness contracts, with exact event-set assertions.
Independent Python fcntl checks for private descriptor flag bits and exec inheritance; only the selected fixture FD is inspected.
exclusions: There is no matching GNU command-line implementation for persistent descriptor semantics, so runnable checks are honest contract cases rather than parity cases.
No real or host network target is used. TCP and UDP peer behavior is deferred to a future disposable network fixture.
No signal is generated. signalfd mask ownership is deferred to a future disposable process fixture.
The runner has no setup hook for injected socketpair or PTY descriptors; only Bash-created private pipes are used for bounded wait checks.
The case count exceeds the preferred range to retain original coverage and isolate independent additional edge cases.

cases.purpose: Bash's type -t contract identifies a compiled-in loadable as a builtin, even with an empty executable PATH.
Check that Bash help exposes the advertised API and the key wait/readiness descriptor contract documented by bashpoll_doc.
cases.script:
doc=$(help bashpoll) || exit 1
for item in \
  'bashpoll listen ADDR:PORT' \
  'bashpoll listen-unix /path/sock FDVAR' \
  'bashpoll listen-udp ADDR:PORT FDVAR' \
  'bashpoll send-udp HOST:PORT' \
  'bashpoll recv-udp FD' \
  'bashpoll accept LISTEN_FD FDVAR' \
  'bashpoll connect HOST:PORT' \
  'bashpoll wait [-t TIMEOUT_MS]' \
  'bashpoll close FD' \
  'bashpoll set-nonblock FD on|off' \
  'bashpoll clear-cloexec FD' \
  'bashpoll signalfd SIG... FDVAR' \
  'FDVAR receives the new fd in the caller' \
  'Bare FDs request read readiness'; do
  [[ $doc == *"$item"* ]] || exit 2
done
printf 'help contract ok\n'

cases.purpose: Use a private Bash process-substitution pipe to verify zero-timeout empty output for read interest and the documented writable event for explicit write interests.
cases.script:
exec {probe}> >(while IFS= read -r line; do :; done)
quiet=$(bashpoll wait -t 0 "$probe") || exit 1
write=$(bashpoll wait -t 0 "$probe:write") || exit 2
read_write=$(bashpoll wait -t 0 "$probe:read,write") || exit 3
[[ -z $quiet ]] || exit 4
[[ $write == "$probe writable" ]] || exit 5
[[ $read_write == "$probe writable" ]] || exit 6
exec {probe}>&-
printf 'quiet=empty;write=writable;read-write=writable\n'

cases.purpose: A private pipe whose writer exits with no queued bytes reports EPOLLHUP; bashpoll maps that event to its documented hup label.
cases.script:
exec {eof}< <(:)
observed=$(bashpoll wait -t 1000 "$eof") || exit 1
[[ $observed == "$eof hup" ]] || exit 2
exec {eof}<&-
printf 'eof=hup\n'

cases.purpose: The documented parser rejects an invalid timeout, invalid readiness suffix, and unknown subcommand with Bash's conventional EX_USAGE status 2.
cases.script:
if bashpoll wait -t nope 3; then exit 1; else timeout_status=$?; fi
if bashpoll wait -t 0 3:invalid; then exit 2; else interest_status=$?; fi
if bashpoll __suite_unknown_subcommand__; then exit 3; else command_status=$?; fi
[[ $timeout_status == 2 && $interest_status == 2 && $command_status == 2 ]] || exit 4
printf 'usage-errors=2,2,2\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise TCP listen, accept, connect, data exchange, timeout and close behavior with a bounded private peer.
cases.reason: The existing tcp and tcp-client peers can drive all of this on 127.0.0.1; only cases are missing.

cases.purpose: Exercise listen-unix and accept, relative socket-path creation and cleanup, stale socket replacement, and refusal to unlink a non-socket entry.
cases.reason: Everything except cleanup is observable with a python3 AF_UNIX client helper inside one per-side script; cleanup on close is not implemented by the candidate.

cases.purpose: Exercise listen-udp, send-udp and recv-udp with empty and binary datagrams, timeout, source-address reporting, and hex output.
cases.reason: The existing udp (echo) and udp-client peers cover send/receive on loopback; no cases exist.

cases.purpose: Exercise signalfd delivery, accepted signal names, overlapping masks, close/unload restoration, preblocked signals, and invalid signal handling.
cases.reason: No fixture sends signals; the fixture shell can signal itself inside the disposable VM and read SigBlk from /proc/$BASHPID/status. Unload restoration is unreachable for the compiled-in builtin.

cases.purpose: Socket/PTY descriptor behavior and failure injection beyond the runnable private FIFO flag, inheritance and close coverage.
cases.reason: FIFO behavior is covered; socket and PTY descriptors are creatable in the VM (loopback peers, python3 pty helper) but no fixture exists.

cases.purpose: Socket half-close/error and PTY readiness beyond the runnable simultaneous private FIFO readiness contract.
cases.reason: FIFO readiness is covered; socket half-close/RST and PTY readiness need a controlled peer, which loopback helpers can provide.

cases.script:
mkfifo private-pipe
exec {probe}<> private-pipe
bashpoll set-nonblock "$probe" on
bashpoll clear-cloexec "$probe"
command -p python3 -c 'import fcntl,os,sys; assert fcntl.fcntl(int(sys.argv[1]),fcntl.F_GETFL)&os.O_NONBLOCK; print("nonblock=on;inherited=yes")' "$probe"
printf 'queued\n' >&"$probe"
observed=$(bashpoll wait -t 0 "$probe:read")
[[ $observed == "$probe readable" ]]
IFS= read -r row <&"$probe"
[[ $row == queued ]]
bashpoll set-nonblock "$probe" off
command -p python3 -c 'import fcntl,os,sys; assert not (fcntl.fcntl(int(sys.argv[1]),fcntl.F_GETFL)&os.O_NONBLOCK); print("nonblock=off")' "$probe"
bashpoll close "$probe"
if bashpoll wait -t 0 "$probe"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'ready=readable;payload=queued;closed-status=%s\n' "$rc"
cases.purpose: A private FIFO opened read/write permits readiness, payload consumption and close tests without peer scheduling. Independent Python fcntl checks observe on/off O_NONBLOCK bits and exec inheritance of the selected private descriptor after clear-cloexec.

cases.script:
mkfifo first second
exec {one}<> first
exec {two}<> second
printf 'first\n' >&"$one"
printf 'second\n' >&"$two"
observed=$(bashpoll wait -t 0 "$one" "$two")
count=0
while IFS=' ' read -r fd event; do
 [[ $event == readable ]]
 case $fd in "$one") [[ ${seen_one:-0} == 0 ]]; seen_one=1 ;; "$two") [[ ${seen_two:-0} == 0 ]]; seen_two=1 ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
 count=$((count+1))
done <<< "$observed"
[[ $count == 2 && $seen_one == 1 && $seen_two == 1 ]]
bashpoll close "$one"
bashpoll close "$two"
printf 'both private FIFOs readable exactly once\n'
cases.stdout: both private FIFOs readable exactly once
cases.purpose: Both bounded private FIFO descriptors must be reported exactly once; event ordering is unspecified by epoll and no payload or event label is normalized.
